source_checks.finding: Modern US English uses adjective alternate for UK/general alternative and noun alternate for a substitute/deputy, in addition to the alternating/every-second meanings.

Current learner-dictionary treatment marks anger as a transitive verb meaning 'make someone angry'; the Current intransitive L2 'anger at sth/sb = become angry' should not be promoted as an ordinary active branch.

relation_decisions.target_truth: alter vs alert may remain a low-friction spelling/form boundary if useful, but Current is internally factually contradictory: same_normalized_pronunciation=true while its own phonetics differ. Do not default it to high-priority A merely because edit distance is small; learner priority should depend on real confusion risk.

Keep the alternative↔alternate boundary, but encode regional variation: alternative is the general choice/substitute adjective/noun; alternate also means alternating/every second, while US English additionally uses alternate as adjective/noun for an alternative/substitute. Current relation incorrectly presents those meanings as mutually exclusive.
Keep aluminum vs aluminium as regional spelling variants of the same chemical element: aluminum is standard American English; aluminium is standard British/international English.

decisions.target_truth: Restore ordinary alter=change/make different as the main high-value verb. Specialist veterinary alter=neuter/spay is valid but lower reference/recognition and must not be the sole Active sense while Core says '改变'. Reassess the alter↔alert relation separately.

Preserve verb alternate=take turns/change repeatedly and adjective alternate=every other/every second. Add modern US adjective alternate=alternative/substitute and noun alternate=substitute/deputy/backup at appropriate recognition depth. Current Truth is incomplete without this regional branch.

Keep ordinary altitude=height above sea/ground level as the main learner meaning. Geometry altitude=perpendicular from a vertex is a valid specialist term but belongs in reference/recognition rather than equal main Active depth for general English.

Keep always=at all times/on every occasion as the core. Preserve pragmatic fallback use 'you can always...' = in any event/as an available option. 'As always' means as usual and belongs to the ordinary frequency branch, not as evidence for the fallback/any-event branch.

Use one main noun center: a person who does an activity for enjoyment rather than as a profession, plus adjective nonprofessional. 'Amateur athlete' is an instance of that nonprofessional meaning, not a separate lexical sense. Recognize the evaluative extension amateur=unskilled/inexperienced as a contextual negative nuance rather than a redundant dictionary split.

Use one semantic center: strong desire/goal to achieve something, especially success, position, power or another important outcome. Positive 'ambition' and negative 'political/power ambition' are largely contextual/connotative realizations rather than clean independent noun senses. Preserve productive patterns such as ambition to do sth / ambition for sth as appropriate.

Keep noun amount=quantity/total and high-value phrasal verb amount to=total/be equivalent to. Represent amount to once as one coherent lexical branch plus its canonical pattern; Current duplicates the same object as an Active sense, a secondary_sense, and two construction facts.

Keep general analysis=detailed examination/breakdown/reasoning as the learner center. Literary analysis is a domain application of that general meaning, not an independent lexical sense 'a form of literary criticism in which structure is analyzed'; demote/remove that subtype as a separate Active branch.

Keep general analytic=relating to/using analysis or logical reasoning as the main adjective. Analytic geometry and linguistics analytic language are legitimate specialist terms but belong in reference/recognition rather than equal main Active L2/L3 depth for general English.

Broaden beyond a human person: ancestor can be a person, animal, plant or ancestral organism from which a later individual/group descends, and can extend to a predecessor/forerunner of a later thing. Current person-only definition is too narrow for high-value academic/evolutionary reading.

Keep adjective ancient=belonging to remote history / very old as the main learner map. Noun 'the ancients'=people of ancient times is valid but lower-frequency recognition/reference, not equal main Active depth.

Keep conjunction and as the function-word core and explicit high-value structures such as and so on where useful. Do not store lexicalized idioms such as bread and butter=livelihood as ordinary collocation evidence for the semantic core of and; such idioms require their own phrase-level ownership/layer.

Keep noun anger as the main meaning and transitive verb anger sb=make someone angry as a legitimate lower branch. Remove/demote Current intransitive 'anger at sth/sb = become angry' from ordinary Active Knowledge; current learner dictionaries mark the verb transitive. Keep noun patterns anger at/over sth and in anger. A specialized idiom 'in anger' meaning in a real/serious use context may remain separate reference knowledge if later judged worthwhile.

Center the learner map on physical angle and high-value familiar-new noun angle=perspective/way of considering a subject. Keep angle for sth=try indirectly to obtain as a useful construction. Physical position/move-at-angle verbs may be lower. Historic ethnonym Angles belongs in reference only and must not sit in Core/main Active alongside ordinary angle.

Keep ordinary angry at/about/with as the main adjective. Literary violent-elements use (angry waves/weather) and medical-looking inflamed/red 'angry wound' are valid extensions but low-value recognition/reference, not equal main learner-active depth.

Restore noun anguish=extreme mental or physical suffering as the main Active meaning; Current Core already states this while Active senses are empty. Verb anguish/suffer anguish may be lower recognition where contemporary; rare causative 'anguish sb' must not displace the noun core.
